name: closing_auction_anticipation_5s
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: NSE's closing auction (15:30-15:40) concentrates 5-8% of daily volume. Stocks trending in a direction during the last 30 minutes tend to continue into the close as index fund rebalancing, mutual fund NAV-related orders, and institutional closing trades cluster. By entering at 15:00 in the direction of the last-30-min trend, you capture the closing auction premium. Edge persists because the closing auction mechanism creates a structural demand pattern that retail traders can't exploit (they flatten by 15:15).
mechanism: Order flow imbalance between aggressive buyers and sellers creates short-term price pressure. When buy-side aggression exceeds sell-side by a threshold, the order book tilts and market makers adjust their quotes upward. This creates a 15-45 second drift before the book rebalances as new limit orders arrive to capture the improved price.

indicators.name: vwap_dist_pct
indicators.purpose: are we above or below VWAP

filters.expiry_filter: skip on expiry day (closing auction dynamics change)

weaknesses: Very short hold (29 bars max) — edge per trade is thin; need high frequency to compound
Closing 30 min can be unpredictable on news days — institutional flow gets disrupted
Must flatten by 15:29 — can't capture the actual auction premium without overnight exposure
prior_art: Closing auction premium — documented in market microstructure literature (Pagano et al.)
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
